question: After allowing a discount of 28%, an article is available for ₹3,240. Its marked price is _______.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the Marked Price be 100%. After allowing a 28% discount, the Selling Price = 100% − 28% = 72%.

We are given that 72% corresponds to ₹3,240.

1% corresponds to 3240 ÷ 72 = ₹45

Marked Price (100%) = 45 × 100 = ₹4,500

**∴ The correct answer is ₹4,500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Selling Price (SP) = ₹3,240

Discount Percentage = 28%

**Formula Used:**

Marked Price (MP) = (SP × 100) ÷ (100 − Discount%)

 
 
 
 SP = 72%
 Discount = 28%
 
 ₹3,240
 Marked Price = 100% = ?
 
 
• 
 
• 
 
• 
 

 

**Calculations:**

⇒ MP = (3240 × 100) ÷ (100 − 28)

⇒ MP = 324000 ÷ 72

⇒ MP = 4500

**∴ The correct answer is ₹4,500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price and Discount

Discount is always given on the Marked Price (MP) of an article. Selling Price (SP) is obtained after deducting the discount from the Marked Price.

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts of x% and y% are allowed, then Equivalent Single Discount = x + y − (x × y) ÷ 100.

Profit/Loss Percentage

Unlike discount which acts on Marked Price, Profit or Loss is always calculated on the Cost Price (CP). Profit % = [(SP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100.
